Masayoshi Son’s $20 million bet on Alibaba became one of the greatest venture capital investments in history. 💰 In 2000, Son met a relatively unknown Jack Ma and reportedly spent only a few minutes with him before deciding to invest. Instead of relying entirely on financial projections, Son believed in Ma’s vision and the potential of his company. SoftBank eventually secured roughly a 30% stake in Alibaba. What started as a $20 million investment later became worth billions as Alibaba grew into one of the world’s biggest technology companies. Interestingly, Son initially wanted to invest $40 million, but Jack Ma reportedly accepted only $20 million because he believed that was enough to build the business. The lesson? Sometimes the biggest investments are made before the numbers look obvious. Would you invest based on a founder’s vision—or wait for the financial data to prove it? The Alibaba Illusion — Why the Price You See Online is a Never the Real Price Is that $0.50 price tag on Alibaba a scam? No, but it is an illusion. 🛑 Stop treating B2B platforms like an Amazon retail store. Alibaba is an incredibly powerful tool for product discovery and small businesses, but the prices you see are a matrix of conditions. If you want the lowest price, you have to meet the factory's physics: massive volume, standard materials, and domestic specs. When testing an idea, paying a markup for low MOQs and English support is a fair deal.
